title: Life Path Constellation
tagline: A 10-year life plan turned into a game you actually reopen.
summary: An interactive constellation map that turns a five-pillar life plan — spirituality, career, finance, relationships, health — into something explorable instead of a document written once and forgotten. Check off goals, add your own, and carry progress between sessions with a portable save file — no backend required.

audienceHooks.recruiter: Solo-shipped an interactive data product — modeling, accessible SVG visualization, client-side state — tested end to end.
audienceHooks.consultant: A working demo of turning an abstract strategy framework into a tool people actually keep using.

role: Sole designer & builder — concept, information design, interaction design, accessibility, and implementation.

caseStudy.problem: A five-pillar life plan (spirituality, career, finance, relationships, health) mapped across now/5-year/10-year horizons existed only as a static written doc — easy to draft once and easy to never open again.
approach: Modeled each pillar as a branch of a radial 'skill tree' / constellation, with three time-horizon stars per branch radiating out from a central 'you are here' hub.

Applied a colorblind-safe, contrast-validated categorical color system — checked with a validator script rather than eyeballed — so each pillar reads as a distinct identity in both the visual map and a plain-text accessible table view.
Built a client-side goal-tracking layer: checkboxes, custom goal entry, per-star progress rings, and an overall progress bar.
Replaced browser storage with an explicit save/load file, so progress is portable across devices and never silently disappears.
QA'd every state — desktop, mobile, post-interaction, save/load round-trip — with headless-browser screenshot testing before calling it done.
caseStudy.solution: A single self-contained HTML file that opens instantly with no install or server: an interactive constellation map (or a plain accessible table, toggled with one click) where goals can be checked off, new ones added per pillar, and progress exported to and restored from a small JSON file.

caseStudy.learnings: Building under a strict no-browser-storage constraint initially felt like a limitation — it ended up being the better design for a personal tool meant to be reopened across devices: an exportable save file is more trustworthy than invisible local state that can quietly reset.
